title: B/R Unveils 2026 College Football Top 25 After Week 9: Expert Rankings Reveal Surprises
body:
The week‑nine slate of college football delivered a shocker that will reverberate through the remainder of the season: the USC Trojans toppled a heavily favored Ohio State Buckeyes squad, sending ripples across the Top 25 and reshaping the narrative for both programs. The upset, combined with a slew of close contests and surprising performances, forced a major reshuffle in the latest B/R Experts Top 25 rankings, highlighting the volatility that has come to define this year’s campaign.

USC’s victory over the Buckeyes was the headline‑making moment, but the ripple effects extended far beyond Los Angeles. In the updated rankings, the Trojans vaulted into the upper tier, cementing their status as a legitimate contender for the conference crown. Ohio State, meanwhile, slipped several spots, a stark reminder that even perennial powerhouses are vulnerable when execution falters. The Trojans’ win was anchored by a balanced offensive attack that blended a revitalized ground game with efficient passing, while Ohio State’s defense, traditionally a bastion of strength, struggled to contain the Trojan rush and succumbed to critical turnovers in the second half.

Equally noteworthy is the movement of Tennessee, which climbed to fourth in the poll with a 6‑2 record after a gritty win that showcased the Volunteers’ resilience. The Volunteers, however, remain plagued by inconsistency at quarterback. True freshman Faizon Brandon, who has shown flashes of poise, continues to wrestle with the pressures of leading a storied program. Tennessee’s upcoming clash with Kentucky will serve as a litmus test for Brandon’s development and the team’s ability to sustain momentum against a disciplined SEC opponent. Analysts point to the Volunteers’ defensive front, which has been among the nation’s best at limiting yards after contact, as a potential stabilizing factor if the offense can find rhythm.

The mid‑week rankings also reflected the ascendance of several non‑Power Five programs that have been quietly amassing quality wins. Teams such as Boise State and Cincinnati have re‑entered the Top 25, rewarding their disciplined play and strategic coaching. Their rise underscores a broader trend: depth and tactical adaptability are increasingly outweighing raw talent alone. Defensive schematics, in particular, have become a differentiator, with many of the surprise victors employing hybrid fronts that confuse traditional offensive line assignments.

Conversely, some traditional heavyweights have slipped further down the list. Michigan, despite a solid record, fell out of the top ten after a lackluster performance against a struggling opponent, raising questions about their offensive line’s ability to protect a quarterback who has been intermittently effective. Meanwhile, the ACC’s Clemson Tigers, once a fixture at the summit, found themselves outside the top fifteen after a narrow defeat that exposed vulnerabilities in their secondary. These declines illustrate the unforgiving nature of a season where a single misstep can erode years of program prestige.

Looking ahead, the reshaped Top 25 sets the stage for a dramatic second half of the season. USC’s newfound confidence will be tested in the Pac‑12 championship race, while Ohio State must regroup quickly to avoid a slide that could jeopardize their College Football Playoff aspirations. Tennessee’s quarterback situation will be under the microscope as they head into a pivotal SEC showdown, and the emerging non‑Power Five contenders will aim to solidify their legitimacy with marquee wins. As the calendar turns toward the conference championships, the fluidity of this year’s rankings suggests that the path to the postseason will be anything but predictable, promising fans a continuation of the high‑stakes drama that has defined week nine.
